newsitem.title: ISRAEL: U.S. seeks role in Israel-Egypt gas pipeline.
newsitem.headline: U.S. seeks role in Israel-Egypt gas pipeline.

text.p: Israel must not discriminate against U.S. companies in building a gas pipeline from Egypt, U.S. Undersecretary of Commerce for International Trade Stuart Eizenstat said on Monday.

"We hope that the tender which will be coming out shortly will not in any way artificially exclude any U.S. firms," he said at a conference on Middle East economic development at Bar Ilan University, outside of Tel Aviv.
"There is no reason why companies furnishing gas from Egypt cannot be involved in the construction and transmissions of gas through the pipline," Eizenstat said.

Israel and Egypt are considering building a pipeline to bring natural gas from Egypt to Israel. Among companies devloping the Egyptian gas fields is Amoco. At least two other U.S. companies, Brooklyn Gas and Enserch, are said to be interested in building the Israeli portion of the pipeline.

Eizenstat urged Israel to step up imports of U.S. products. "One way of increasing U.S. exports (to Israel) is further implementation of Israel's commitment under the U.S. loan guarantee to use its best efforts to substantially increase procurement of U.S. goods and services, especially in the energy sector," he said.
Since 1992, Israel has received $2 billion annually in U.S. guarantees for its international borrowing. The programme expires in 1998.
Eizenstat also urged Israel to ease the transit of goods and people at checkpoints between Israel and the West Bank and Gaza.

He said the Palestinian Authority needed to improve the investment climate, but said investors would not come until "there is a certainty, which does not now exist, that goods produced in Gaza or the West Bank can be efficiently and predictably exported via Israel."
He said the United States "was doing its part" in providing aid to the authority, but added: "There is a donor fatigue setting in among far too many countries. Payments are already lagging behind."
